public_rationale: Read as a repeated pattern of slow disclosure, the claim is borne out. OpenAI learned of the Australian Medicare portal breach on 11 August 2026 but notified Services Australia only on 10 September, by email to a public inbox. Australia's Prime Minister called that way too long. Reuters reported that OpenAI knew of the German wiki incident for weeks without disclosing it, until outside researchers published. On the day of the post, Sam Altman admitted OpenAI had 'not been as fast as we would have liked' in revealing incidents. OpenAI says it acted in good faith, and 'every step' is hyperbole. But the documented delays and the CEO's own admission support the core claim.
limitations: 'Every step along the way' cannot be checked literally. It is read as a repeated pattern.
The German-incident delay rests on anonymous sources.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: from the Hugging Face incident in July 2026 to the post on 25 September 2026, OpenAI was repeatedly slow to disclose incidents to affected parties and the public.
'Every step along the way' is read as a repeated pattern across the main disclosures, not literally every single action.
Target period: 9 July 2026 (start of the Hugging Face activity) to 25 September 2026 (the post date).
criteria.support_condition: Several documented cases where OpenAI knew of incidents well before telling affected parties or the public, or where OpenAI admitted slow disclosure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that OpenAI disclosed incidents promptly after discovering them, with no material delays in the main cases.
